candidates.exact_span: A written submission shall be provided within 5 days of the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when a written noncompliance report was required depends on when the permittee became aware; different awareness dates or interpretations of triggering circumstances change which FY2025 reporting obligations apply and whether absent written reports indicate missing required evidence versus no obligation.

candidates.exact_span: The period of noncompliance including exact dates and times, and if the noncompliance has not been corrected, the anticipated time it is expected to continue
candidates.computation_change_reason: Required report content defines the temporal scope of documented noncompliance; interpreting what must be reported (including uncorrected periods) affects whether monitoring or discharge periods without numeric results are established no-discharge intervals, documented noncompliance spans, or unresolved missing-evidence cases.

candidates.exact_span: Any unanticipated bypass which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'unanticipated bypass' and whether an exceedance of 'any effluent limitation' occurred determines which enforceable limits are implicated for comparison, whether 24-hour reporting was required, and whether event-conditioned monitoring or reporting gaps reflect required-but-unmet obligations versus inapplicable conditions.

candidates.exact_span: Any upset which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a discharge event qualifies as an 'upset' that exceeded an effluent limitation changes which limits are treated as exceeded for compliance comparison, triggers 24-hour reporting obligations, and shapes how missing results during upset periods are classified.

candidates.exact_span: Violation of a maximum daily discharge limitation for any of the pollutants listed by the Director in Part II (industrial permits only) of the permit to be reported within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties 24-hour reporting to maximum daily discharge limitations in Part II and limits that scope to industrial permits; interpreting industrial-permit applicability, which Part II pollutants are listed, and what constitutes a maximum daily discharge limitation changes which numeric limits are enforceable for comparison and which exceedances carried a distinct reporting obligation in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The Director may waive the written report on a case-by-case basis if the oral report has been received within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A waiver can substitute oral for written reporting; whether a waiver was granted or oral reporting sufficed changes whether missing written submissions indicate an unmet monitoring/reporting obligation or a satisfied, waived requirement.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall institute a program within 12 months of the effective date of the permit (or continue an existing one) directed towards optimizing the efficiency and extending the useful life of the facility.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 12-month deadline measured from the permit effective date determines whether the pollution-prevention program obligation was applicable during all or part of Federal FY2025 and whether related compliance expectations were in force.

candidates.exact_span: The effluent quality and plant performance;
candidates.computation_change_reason: As a required program consideration item, interpretation of whether 'shall consider' effluent quality implies assessment or monitoring obligations affects which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable for FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Bypasses and overflows of the tributary sewerage system and treatment works;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Required consideration of bypasses and overflows interacts with separate bypass reporting rules; interpreting whether evaluation of these events is mandatory affects monitoring obligations and how periods involving bypass/overflow without numeric results are classified.
